extra.message: The 'outputType' query parameter (from request.query) is interpolated into a shell command string executed with spawn(cmd, [], { shell: true }). The format value is not validated against an allowlist, allowing command injection via a crafted outputType (e.g. 'gzip; cat /etc/passwd'). Note the sibling endpoint /api/regions/:id/coverage-export validates its preset against ALLOWED_PRESETS, confirming this omission.

The public /api/auth/register endpoint accepts a 'role' field from the request body and inserts it directly (role: role || 'customer'). A client can self-register with role 'ops_admin', 'dispatcher', or 'field_worker' to gain elevated privileges, because no allowlist or server-side default is enforced.

PATCH /api/customers/:id/account-settings only requires authentication and performs Object.assign(customer, request.body) then updates with the full merged object. There is no role or ownership check, and arbitrary columns (including 'userId' and 'isActive') can be overwritten. Any authenticated user can modify any customer record and reassign its userId (e.g. to themselves) to take over another customer's jobs and data.

extra.message: The multipart upload filename (data.filename) is passed directly to resolve(archiveDir, data.filename) without path.basename() or sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g. a filename of '../../../../something') to write files outside the intended incident-archive directory. The sibling /api/workers/:id/certifications endpoint correctly applies path.basename(), confirming this omission.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: The 'templateName' query parameter is joined into the filesystem path via path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, templateName) with no basename() or prefix validation, then read and returned. A templateName such as '../../../../etc/passwd' allows arbitrary file read (path traversal) by any ops_admin.

extra.message: The uploaded filename (data.filename) is passed directly to resolve(iconDir, data.filename) and written without basename() sanitization, allowing path traversal to write arbitrary files outside the service-icons directory.

extra.message: The webhook test-delivery endpoint reads the callback URL from the client-controlled 'x-webhook-callback' header and passes it directly to fetch(). An ops_admin can be induced to make the server send requests to arbitrary internal/loopback addresses (SSRF).

The 'uid' query parameter is interpolated directly into an LDAP filter string '(uid=${uid})' without escaping. This is an LDAP injection. The codebase defines an escapeDirectoryFilter() helper and uses it in /api/workers/directory-lookup, but omits it here, confirming the oversight.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: GET /api/workers/:id requires only authentication and returns the worker profile with 'user: true', which includes the full users row including the 'passwordHash' column. Any authenticated user (including customers) can enumerate worker IDs and retrieve bcrypt password hashes.
GET /api/admin/workers returns workerProfiles with 'user: true', which includes the users.passwordHash column. Password hashes are returned to the client instead of being stripped.

In GET /api/jobs/:id, incidents are fetched without any role filtering and returned in full to the client. A customer viewing their own job therefore receives each incident's 'internalNotes' and 'assignedTo' fields, leaking internal-only data that should not be visible to customers.

GET /api/incidents/:id filters messages for customers but returns the full incident object ({ ...incident, messages }), which includes 'internalNotes'. A customer with access to the incident's job can read internal incident notes.

GET /api/incidents returns enriched incident objects (with all columns, including 'internalNotes') to customers whose jobs have incidents. The customer scope is applied only to the WHERE filter, not to the returned columns.

GET /api/proofs/:id/download checks that a customer only sees customer-visible proofs, but does not verify the proof's job belongs to the requesting customer. A customer can download any customer-visible proof document by ID across all customers (IDOR). The related GET /api/proofs has the same gap.

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/:id/rate-detail requires only authentication. Passing ?dataLevel=full returns the job's 'internalNotes' and priority to any authenticated user with no role or ownership check, exposing internal-only cost/notes data.

POST /api/jobs/:id/notice-preview compiles a user-supplied 'templateBody' with Handlebars.compile(templateBody). This is a server-side template injection (SSTI) allowing the caller to evaluate arbitrary template expressions against the compiled context (e.g. accessing prototype/constructor chains).

extra.message: GET /api/partners/tracking-widget/:jobId is unauthenticated and reflects the request Origin header back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without validation. extra.message: A hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret ('field-dispatch-dev-jwt-secret-change-in-production') is used when JWT_SECRET is unset. If deployed without the environment variable, an attacker can forge valid JWTs for any role and bypass authentication.

GET /api/routes/:id has no role or ownership checks. Any authenticated user (including customers) can read any route along with all its stops and the associated jobs with customer and location data. extra.message: GET /api/workers requires only authentication and returns every active field worker's name, email, and phone to any authenticated user, including customers. This exposes PII with no business need.

GET /api/customers returns all customers (company name, contact name, email, phone, notes) to any non-customer authenticated role. Field workers and dispatchers can enumerate all customers and their contact/notes data without restriction.

extra.message: The AES encryption keys for route plan snapshots and worker check-in payloads are derived from hardcoded fallback secrets ('dispatch-route-plan-key' and 'field-checkin-payload-key') when the corresponding environment variables are unset, allowing an attacker to decrypt/forge snapshots.
JWTs are signed without an expiry (app.jwt.sign({ id, role }) has no expiresIn). Tokens remain valid indefinitely, increasing the window of exposure if a token is leaked.

POST /api/workers/onboard-account accepts a client-supplied 'costFactor' and passes it to bcrypt.hash(password, costFactor || 4). An excessively large value causes CPU-intensive hashing (DoS), while a small value weakens the hash; the parameter is not constrained to a safe range.
